Subject: Re: Fwd: Qorix checkout: sudden latency spike, 5% errors since 08:50

Quick update from triage (initial):
- What we see: sustained elevation in token-gen tail latency and increased 5xxs originating from the inference tier (service: inference-gateway-us-west).
- Hypothesis: concurrent background kernel rebalances + NVMe GC on a subset of nodes leading to IO wait; also seeing a small spike in OOM-kills on one pod, which triggered transient routing flaps.

Immediate mitigations applied (10:00–10:04 PT):
1) Temporarily added two extra inference instances to Qorix's routed pool and pinned traffic so their requests bypass the autoscaler ramp.
2) Enabled smaller-model fallback (gpt-lite-6b) for requests over 2s latency threshold so we preserve throughput for checkout flows.
3) Increased retry-window and enabled aggressive KV prefix caching for common checkout prompts (pre-baked cache keys).

Impact so far: error rate dropped from ~5% to ~1.4%; median latency back to ~1.6x baseline, p99 improving but not yet stable.

Next steps (ETA):
- 10:30 PT: complete IO health check and evict noisy instance(s) if needed.
- 11:00 PT: determine whether a model kernel rollback or NVMe maintenance window is required.
- 13:00 PT: exec sync (Michael to host) — recommended attendance: Michael, Laura, Qorix execs.

Attachment: runbook reference — https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/ops-playbooks (internal)

Monica
